name: Ark

global_influences.evidence: Ark emerged as part of the same 1990s hard-rock wave as LRB and Nagar Baul, together forming the 'Big Three of Rock' credited with popularizing rock music in Bangladesh, implying a shared set of Western rock reference points typical of the era's cassette/import exposure.

local_adaptation_notes: Ark's debut album মুক্তিযুদ্ধ (Muktijuddho, 'Liberation War,' 1991) directly engaged national historical memory as subject matter for a hard rock album, paralleling Cryptic Fate's later similar thematic choice; the band's 1996 breakthrough single 'Sweety' (from Tajmahal) became one of the most enduring staples of Bangladeshi rock, demonstrating the genre's capacity for mass commercial crossover.
sound_evolution_summary: Founding period (1991): formed by keyboardist Ashiquzzaman Tulu with Ridwan Nabi Pancham and Shamim; debut album মুক্তিযুদ্ধ engaged Liberation War themes. Breakthrough period (1996): second album Tajmahal, released via Soundtek, was a phenomenal commercial success driven by the single 'Sweety,' cementing Ark's status as one of the most popular rock bands of the 1990s. Later period: continued releases across five studio albums plus contributed compilation tracks, sustaining the band's presence within the mainstream rock canon.
concert_culture_notes: As part of the 'Big Three of Rock' era, Ark benefited from the same 1990s expansion of large-scale Bangladeshi rock concert culture that elevated LRB and Nagar Baul to national prominence.
listener_community_notes: Core member of the foundational 'Big Three of Rock' listener ecosystem (with Nagar Baul and LRB) that defined 1990s Bangladeshi rock fandom; 'Sweety' remains a rock-culture touchstone recognized across generations.
